title: The Mother Who Changed: A Story of Dementia

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收看《重构者》，这是一档专注于对设计的热爱及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜总会当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每晚你都要带300件你最珍贵的藏品去上班，你把DJ台变成了一个充满美丽50年历史艺术品的活的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在可以在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Amongst philosophers who study dementia, there's this story that gets told over and over again, and it's about a woman named Margot.
sentences.zh: 在研究痴呆症的哲学家中，流传着这样一个被反复讲述的故事，讲的是一个叫玛戈的女人。

sentences.en: Margot was a 55-year-old woman who suffered from early-onset Alzheimer's disease.
sentences.zh: 玛戈是一名55岁的女性，患有早发性阿尔茨海默病。

sentences.en: She couldn't recognize anyone around her.
sentences.zh: 她认不出身边任何人。

sentences.en: She spent her days painting and listening to music.
sentences.zh: 她每天的时间都在画画和听音乐中度过。

sentences.en: She read mystery novels too, often the same book day after day.
sentences.zh: 她也读悬疑小说，经常日复一日地读同一本书。

sentences.en: The mystery always remained mysterious because she would forget it.
sentences.zh: 谜团永远是个谜，因为她会忘掉它。

sentences.en: But despite her illness, or maybe even because of it, Margot was very happy.
sentences.zh: 但尽管患有疾病，或者也许正是因为这种疾病，玛戈非常快乐。

sentences.en: The Margot story presents philosophers with this riddle.
sentences.zh: 玛戈的故事给哲学家们提出了这样一个谜题。

sentences.en: Imagine that years ago, when Margot was fully competent, she wrote out a formal document explaining that if she ever developed Alzheimer's disease,
sentences.zh: 假设多年前，当玛戈完全具备民事行为能力时，她写了一份正式文件，解释说如果她将来患上阿尔茨海默病，

sentences.en: she would not want any life-saving medical treatment, and more than that, she would want to be killed as soon and as painlessly as possible.
sentences.zh: 她不希望接受任何挽救生命的医疗处理，不仅如此，她希望尽可能快、尽可能无痛地被结束生命。

sentences.en: This poses a question.
sentences.zh: 这就提出了一个问题。

sentences.en: Which version of the Margot should be listened to?
sentences.zh: 应该听取哪个版本的玛戈的意见？

sentences.en: The then-Margot before she got sick?
sentences.zh: 生病前那个时候的玛戈？

sentences.en: The then-Margot who never would want to live that way?
sentences.zh: 那个绝不愿意那样生活的玛戈？

sentences.en: Or the now-Margot, who's sitting before us and who is, by all accounts, happy?
sentences.zh: 还是现在坐在我们面前、而且各方面看来都很开心的这个玛戈？

sentences.en: In other words, who is the authentic Margot?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，谁才是真正的玛戈？

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Across the United States, millions of families are confronting a seemingly impossible question.
sentences.zh: 在美国各地，数百万家庭正面临着一个看似不可能回答的问题。

sentences.en: When dementia changes a relative, how much should they accommodate their new personality and their new desires?
sentences.zh: 当痴呆症改变了一个亲人时，他们应该在多大程度上适应其新的个性和新的欲望？

sentences.en: Today, Times Magazine correspondent Katie Engelhardt with one family's experience.
sentences.zh: 今天，《时报杂志》记者凯蒂·恩格尔哈特将带来一个家庭的经历。

sentences.en: It's Friday, January 26th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月26日，星期五。

sentences.en: Katie, how did you first discover this story?
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，你是怎么最初发现这个故事的？

sentences.en: So, I've spent a number of years reporting on issues related to older Americans, and I've been particularly interested in dementia and cognitive impairment.
sentences.zh: 所以，我花了好几年时间报道与老年美国人相关的问题，我一直对痴呆症和认知障碍特别感兴趣。

sentences.en: And this story actually found me, because I've been writing about this subject.
sentences.zh: 这个故事实际上是自己找上门来的，因为我一直在写这个主题。

sentences.en: I was receiving a lot of emails from people who had dementia or whose loved ones had it, and there was one that really stood out to me.
sentences.zh: 我收到了许多来自患有痴呆症或其亲人患有此病的人的电子邮件，其中有一封真的让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: And that was an email from two women, Chris and Julie Norelius, who were writing to tell me the story of their mother.
sentences.zh: 那是两位女性克里斯和朱莉·诺雷利乌斯发来的一封邮件，她们写信来向我讲述她们母亲的故事。

sentences.en: And what was the story that they told you?
sentences.zh: 她们跟你讲的是什么故事？

sentences.en: The story that they described was effectively one of elder abuse.
sentences.zh: 她们所描述的故事实际上是一起虐待老人事件。

sentences.en: In this case, what they were describing wasn't physical abuse or even kind of direct financial abuse, but something a little softer, more like psychological pressure,
sentences.zh: 在这个案例中，她们所描述的不是身体虐待，甚至也不是那种直接的财务虐待，而是一些更温和的东西，更像是心理压力，

sentences.en: more like taking advantage of someone's cognitive weakness in order to convince that person that she wants something she doesn't really.
sentences.zh: 更像是利用某人认知上的弱点，去说服那个人她想要一些她其实并不想要的东西。

sentences.en: But the more I reported on the story, the more complicated it seemed.
sentences.zh: 但随着我对此事的报道深入，它显得越来越复杂。

sentences.en: This wasn't a straightforward story of elder abuse with good guys and bad guys.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一个有着好人和坏人的简单虐待老人事件。

sentences.en: This was a lot more complicated.
sentences.zh: 这要复杂得多。

sentences.en: We can all hear each other?
sentences.zh: 大家都能听到彼此说话吗？

sentences.en: Yeah!
sentences.zh: 能！

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for being willing to chat again.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你们愿意再次聊天。

sentences.en: So the first thing I did was call these sisters, Chris and Julie Norelius, and that really started two years of conversation with them.
sentences.zh: 所以我做的第一件事就是给这对姐妹克里斯和朱莉·诺雷利乌斯打电话，这确实开始了与她们长达两年的对话。

sentences.en: Why don't we just start someplace?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不从某个地方开始聊呢？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Starting someplace works.
sentences.zh: 从某个地方开始就行。

sentences.en: Chris and Julie are separated by a few years, but they act almost like twins.
sentences.zh: 克里斯和朱莉年龄相差几岁，但她们的行为举止几乎就像双胞胎。

sentences.en: And you and I were like, that's enough.
sentences.zh: 而你和我当时都觉得，够了。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Well, look at them.
sentences.zh: 好吧，看看她们。

sentences.en: Wait.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: They look similar.
sentences.zh: 她们看起来很像。

sentences.en: They have virtually the same voice.
sentences.zh: 她们的声音几乎一模一样。

sentences.en: They complete each other's sentences.
sentences.zh: 她们能接上对方的话。

sentences.en: And they told me a lot about their family.
sentences.zh: 她们跟我讲了很多关于她们家庭的事。

sentences.en: The Norelius family grew up in Denison, Iowa, a town of around 8,000 people, surrounded on all sides by cornfields.
sentences.zh: 诺雷利乌斯一家在艾奥瓦州丹尼森长大，这是一个拥有约8,000人口的小镇，四面环绕着玉米地。

sentences.en: Their father, Bill, was sort of a prominent figure around town.
sentences.zh: 她们的父亲比尔可以说是镇上的一个知名人物。

sentences.en: He was a lawyer and a landowner.
sentences.zh: 他是一名律师兼土地所有者。

sentences.en: But we spent most of our time talking about their mother, Diane Norelius.
sentences.zh: 但我们大部分时间都在谈论她们的母亲黛安·诺雷利乌斯。

sentences.en: My mom was really the center of our family.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈真的是我们家庭的中心。

sentences.en: The sisters described their mother as really the backbone of this happy American family.
sentences.zh: 姐妹俩将母亲描述为这个幸福美洲家庭的中流砥柱。

sentences.en: Dad worked all the time.
sentences.zh: 爸爸总是工作。

sentences.en: And so it was up to mom to take care of everything else.
sentences.zh: 所以照顾其他一切事情就成了妈妈的责任。

sentences.en: And it was a great childhood.
sentences.zh: 那是一个美好的童年。

sentences.en: She was confident and, you know, a big presence in the area.
sentences.zh: 她很自信，你知道的，在当地是个很有影响力的人物。

sentences.en: She served on the school board.
sentences.zh: 她曾在学校董事会任职。

sentences.en: She drove a school bus.
sentences.zh: 她开过校车。

sentences.en: She was on the state library board.
sentences.zh: 她是州图书馆委员会成员。

sentences.en: But she was also a very traditional woman.
sentences.zh: 但她也是一个非常传统的女性。

sentences.en: You know, she was a woman of her time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她是个顺应那个时代的女性。

sentences.en: Mom and dad were married in 1957.
sentences.zh: 爸爸妈妈于1957年结婚。

sentences.en: So it was very much a 1950s wife at home with the children, husband working.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常符合1950年代那种妻子在家带孩子、丈夫在外工作的模式。

sentences.en: And she was, by her daughter's admission, quite happy in that role.
sentences.zh: 而且据她女儿承认，她在那个角色中相当快乐。

sentences.en: It was very proper.
sentences.zh: 一切都非常规矩。

sentences.en: And mom took pride in that.
sentences.zh: 妈妈对此感到自豪。

sentences.en: And probably would have continued that way if things hadn't derailed.
sentences.zh: 如果事情没有偏离轨道，大概会一直那样下去吧。

sentences.en: Well, what exactly happened?
sentences.zh: 那么，到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Things for Diane Noreli changed in 2011.
sentences.zh: 黛安·诺雷利乌斯的生活在2011年发生了变化。

sentences.en: Her husband, Bill, died of complications from a broken hip after 53 years of marriage.
sentences.zh: 结婚53年后，她的丈夫比尔因髋部骨折并发症去世。

sentences.en: You have to remember that mom went to nursing school, got out, and pretty much married dad.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，妈妈去读了护理学校，毕业后几乎就嫁给了爸爸。

sentences.en: I mean, she was in her early 20s when she had me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她生我的时候才二十岁出头。

sentences.en: So she had never lived alone, been independent or anything.
sentences.zh: 所以她从未独自生活过，没有独立过或经历过别的什么。

sentences.en: So when she loses this man who has been there for her, her whole life, literally, her adult life, I think she was like loSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，当她失去这个一生中——字面意义上成年后的整个一生——一直陪伴在她身边的男人时，我想她就像迷失了方向。

sentences.en: I mean, she pretended like, don't worry, kids, I'll be fine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她假装成，别担心，孩子们，我会没事的。

sentences.en: But I don't think she knew how to do it by herself, especially without a man.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为她知道该如何独自生活，尤其是没有男人的情况下。

sentences.en: And by do it, you mean live her life like she made it out like, oh, I feel kind of free now and I can go and do anything I want.
sentences.zh: 而你说的“过日子”是指过她自己的生活，她装作，哦，我现在觉得有点自由了，我可以去做任何我想做的事。

sentences.en: But she really didn't.
sentences.zh: 但她其实并没有。

sentences.en: She just watched television.
sentences.zh: 她只是看电视。

sentences.en: And then Diane started losing more people.
sentences.zh: 然后黛安开始失去更多的人。

sentences.en: To me, the next thing was my brother's health crisis.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，接下来发生的是我兄弟的健康危机。

sentences.en: Her son, Eric, died of cancer at 55.
sentences.zh: 她的儿子埃里克在55岁时死于癌症。

sentences.en: That's her only son.
sentences.zh: 那是她唯一的儿子。

sentences.en: That's one of her children.
sentences.zh: 那是她的孩子之一。

sentences.en: Her daughter, Julie, who had lived next door, divorced and moved to Colorado.
sentences.zh: 住在隔壁的女儿朱莉离婚并搬到了科罗拉多州。

sentences.en: Her support group has kind of, to her mind, I think, abandoned her.
sentences.zh: 在她的心目中，她的支持系统似乎已经抛弃了她。

sentences.en: She was seeing herself alone.
sentences.zh: 她发现自己孤身一人。

sentences.en: And then almost all of a sudden, a new man appears in her life.
sentences.zh: 然后几乎毫无预兆地，一个新男人出现在她的生命中。

sentences.en: And then along came Denzel.
sentences.zh: 接着丹泽尔就出现了。

sentences.en: Denzel Nelson.
sentences.zh: 丹泽尔·纳尔逊。

sentences.en: Denzel was known to the family.
sentences.zh: 这个家庭认识丹泽尔。

sentences.en: Denzel Nelson was my father-in-law when I was married to his son.
sentences.zh: 我结婚时，丹泽尔·纳尔逊是我前夫的父亲。

sentences.en: He was actually Julie's ex-husband's father.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是朱莉前夫的父亲。

sentences.en: So a man she'd once been very close with, but hadn't seen much of since her divorce.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个她曾经非常亲近的男人，但自从她离婚后就没怎么见过了。

sentences.en: He always had cowboy boots and a cowboy snap down and a cowboy hat on.
sentences.zh: 他总是穿着牛仔靴，穿着带有牛仔按扣的衬衫，戴着牛仔帽。

sentences.en: He was this kind of stocky cowboy figure.
sentences.zh: 他就是这种有点墩实的牛仔形象。

sentences.en: He'd worked as a horseshoer for most of his life, but had since retired.
sentences.zh: 他大半辈子都以给马钉蹄为生，不过后来退休了。

sentences.en: I mean, it was a completely different image, you know, in comparison to my father.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，与我父亲相比，这是一个完全不同的形象。

sentences.en: I mean, they were, like, opposites.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们就像是截然相反的人。

sentences.en: He was three times divorced.
sentences.zh: 他结过三次婚。

sentences.en: And actually, because he had no finances, he asked if there was any chance he could live in the hired man's house next door to my mom.
sentences.zh: 事实上，因为他没有经济来源，他问有没有可能住在妈妈隔壁雇工住的房子里。

sentences.en: And coming off his last divorce, he'd moved into a little property on the Norellius farm plot.
sentences.zh: 在经历了他最近一次离婚后，他搬进了诺雷利乌斯农场土地上的一个小房产里。

sentences.en: In exchange for helping maintain the yard, like, do the mowing and help out with yard work and things there that he could help with.
sentences.zh: 作为交换，他要帮忙打理庭院，比如割草，帮忙干点他能帮上的院子里的活。

sentences.en: But by all accounts, he and Diane weren't especially close.
sentences.zh: 但据各方所述，他和黛安并不是特别亲近。

sentences.en: Well, she said he was disgusting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她说他很恶心。

sentences.en: He dressed like a hick.
sentences.zh: 他穿得像个乡巴佬。

sentences.en: Mom used the word hick.
sentences.zh: 妈妈用了“乡巴佬”这个词。

sentences.en: And she just thought he was kind of repulsive.
sentences.zh: 她只是觉得他有点让人反感。

sentences.en: She said he smelled bad.
sentences.zh: 她说他身上有难闻的气味。

sentences.en: She said he'd stop by for coffee sometimes.
sentences.zh: 她说他有时会顺道过来喝咖啡。

sentences.en: And she wished that he wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 而她希望他不要来。

sentences.en: So they certainly weren't close by any means.
sentences.zh: 所以他们绝对谈不上亲近。

sentences.en: Until, seemingly out of nowhere, Diane's views on Denzel completely changed.
sentences.zh: 直到，仿佛凭空出现一般，黛安对丹泽尔的看法完全变了。

sentences.en: It was a Sunday.
sentences.zh: 那是一个星期天。

sentences.en: I called mom, and the woman talking to me was not my mom.
sentences.zh: 我打电话给妈妈，跟我说话的那个女人已经不是我妈妈了。

sentences.en: She was like, I need to tell you something.
sentences.zh: 她说，我有些事要告诉你。

sentences.en: And then she went on to say, I've invited Denzel to share my life and live in my house with me.
sentences.zh: 接着她继续说道，我邀请了丹泽尔来分享我的生活，和我一起住在我的房子里。

sentences.en: I'm sure my mouth dropped open because I was like, what is happening?
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定我的下巴都惊掉了，因为我想，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: She goes, I need you to accept him and love him and welcome him into our family because this is what I want.
sentences.zh: 她说，我需要你接受他、爱他并欢迎他加入我们的家庭，因为这是我想要的。

sentences.en: Their mother called them up and sort of presented this as a done deal.
sentences.zh: 她们的母亲打电话给她们，把这事当作一个已经决定的事实来宣布。

sentences.en: Denzel and I are in love.
sentences.zh: 我和丹泽尔恋爱了。

sentences.en: He's moving into the house.
sentences.zh: 他要搬进这所房子。

sentences.en: He's the love of my life.
sentences.zh: 他是我一生的挚爱。

sentences.en: It was hard.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: It was hard to swallow.
sentences.zh: 这很难接受。

sentences.en: It really was.
sentences.zh: 真的很难。

sentences.en: But Chris and Julie tried to be accepting of this.
sentences.zh: 但克里斯和朱莉尽量试着去接受这一点。

sentences.en: You know, for mom's sake, we all adapted.
sentences.zh: 你知道，为了妈妈，我们都做出了调整。

sentences.en: So things were okay for a while.
sentences.zh: 所以有一段时间事情还算顺利。

sentences.en: And Diane, you know, she seemed happy.
sentences.zh: 而且黛安，你知道，她看起来很开心。

sentences.en: She and Denzel started spending their days on these drives.
sentences.zh: 她和丹泽尔开始把时间花在这些驾车出游上。

sentences.en: They'd drive around the state or to different states.
sentences.zh: 他们会开车兜风游历本州或去不同的州。

sentences.en: They'd go to antique shows or horse shows or quilt shows.
sentences.zh: 他们会去看古董展、马展或拼布展。

sentences.en: You know, at age 80, Diane was finding a new way to live.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在80岁的时候，黛安正在寻找一种新的生活方式。

sentences.en: But Diane's daughters also noticed changes in her that they found more worrying.
sentences.zh: 但黛安的女儿们也注意到她身上发生了让她们感到更担忧的变化。

sentences.en: My mom always was a fashionista.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈一直是个时尚达人。

sentences.en: She used to make her own clothing, suits.
sentences.zh: 她过去常常自己做衣服、套装。

sentences.en: Their mother had always been very well dressed, very, you know, interested in her appearance.
sentences.zh: 她们的母亲一直以来都穿得很讲究，你知道的，非常注重自己的外表。

sentences.en: But then I came home and she's wearing jeans with a big, wide cowboy belt.
sentences.zh: 但后来我回家时，她却穿着一条系着宽大牛仔腰带的牛仔裤。

sentences.en: And this old cruddy horse breeder's baseball cap.
sentences.zh: 还戴着一顶破旧的育马者棒球帽。

sentences.en: All of a sudden she was dressing like a cowboy.
sentences.zh: 她突然之间穿得像个牛仔。

sentences.en: And no makeup.
sentences.zh: 而且还不化妆。

sentences.en: No makeup.
sentences.zh: 不化妆。

sentences.en: And I was just like, who are you?
sentences.zh: 我当时就觉得，你到底是谁？

sentences.en: And some of the changes were deeper ones.
sentences.zh: 而且有些变化更加深远。

sentences.en: And she said to me one day, you know, I'm trying to be more assertive.
sentences.zh: 有一天她对我说，你知道的，我在努力变得更有主见。

sentences.en: Denzel's training me to be more assertive.
sentences.zh: 丹泽尔在训练我变得更有主见。

sentences.en: Chris and Julie really felt like their joyful, joyous mother was growing sour.
sentences.zh: 克里斯和朱莉真切地感觉到，她们那位快乐、开朗的母亲正在变得脾气暴躁。

sentences.en: She was being aggressive and mean to people.
sentences.zh: 她对人变得充满攻击性而且很刻薄。

sentences.en: Even Diane's phone calls with her daughters were changing.
sentences.zh: 甚至黛安和女儿们的电话内容也变了。

sentences.en: There started to be this gradual isolation that mom wasn't calling as much.
sentences.zh: 开始出现这种渐进式的疏离，妈妈打电话的次数变少了。

sentences.en: I'd call her and, oh, she'd be busy.
sentences.zh: 我给她打电话，哦，她总是很忙。

sentences.en: I'll have her call you back.
sentences.zh: 我让她给你回电话。

sentences.en: They're finding it harder to reach their mother.
sentences.zh: 她们发现越来越难联系上母亲。

sentences.en: She's not answering the phone.
sentences.zh: 她不接电话。

sentences.en: When she does answer the phone, it seems as if Denzel's always beside her, always sort of coaching her almost on what to say.
sentences.zh: 而当她接电话时，感觉丹泽尔总是待在她身边，几乎总是在一旁指导她该说些什么。

sentences.en: But I think it was harder and harder for her to understand our conversations when we would talk.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，每当我们要聊天时，她想要听懂我们的对话变得越来越难。

sentences.en: They start to feel like their mother is deteriorating in ways they can't quite understand from far away.
sentences.zh: 她们开始觉得，母亲正在以一种她们从远处无法完全理解的方式恶化。

sentences.en: But it's only in September of 2017 that a doctor finally gives shape to what Diane's daughters sort of both knew and couldn't see.
sentences.zh: 但直到2017年9月，医生才终于为黛安的女儿们隐约察觉却又看不真切的情况下了个定论。

sentences.en: I couldn't get a hold of mom and was worried about her.
sentences.zh: 我联系不上妈妈，很担心她。

sentences.en: And I got a phone call from Denzel that said mom was in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 我接到丹泽尔打来的电话，说妈妈住院了。

sentences.en: He didn't think it was her heart.
sentences.zh: 他觉得不是心脏的问题。

sentences.en: They weren't sure.
sentences.zh: 他们也不确定。

sentences.en: Denzel had taken Diane to the emergency room because she felt short of breath.
sentences.zh: 丹泽尔带黛安去了急诊室，因为她觉得呼吸急促。

sentences.en: And at the hospital, she was given a cognitive teSt.
sentences.zh: 在医院里，她接受了一次认知测试。

sentences.en: She scored poorly.
sentences.zh: 她得分很低。

sentences.en: She didn't know the name of the president, for instance.
sentences.zh: 比如，她不知道总统的名字。

sentences.en: I decided, you know what, I'm going back to Iowa and I got a plane ticket.
sentences.zh: 我决定，管他的，我要回爱荷华州，于是我买了一张机票。

sentences.en: Chris actually got a plane ticket, too.
sentences.zh: 克里斯其实也买了一张机票。

sentences.en: But I got back there before Chris.
sentences.zh: 但我比克里斯先回到那里。

sentences.en: So I went to the hospital, met with mom.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了医院，见到了妈妈。

sentences.en: Then Dr. Ingram came in and explained to me that, yeah, you know, your mother, he had diagnosed her with dementia.
sentences.zh: 然后英格拉姆医生进来向我解释说，是的，你知道的，你母亲，他诊断她患上了痴呆症。

sentences.en: And it's here at this time that Diane is diagnosed with dementia.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，黛安被诊断出患有痴呆症。

sentences.en: That was the day we went to Vicki's house.
sentences.zh: 那正是我们去维姬家的一天。

sentences.en: Vicki was kind of a friend to mom and to us.
sentences.zh: 维姬算是妈妈和我们大家的朋友。

sentences.en: And we were so shocked.
sentences.zh: 我们感到极其震惊。

sentences.en: We're sitting at her bar crying.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在她家的吧台旁哭泣。

sentences.en: And she's like, well, of course your mom has dementia.
sentences.zh: 而她说，哦，你妈妈当然有痴呆症啊。

sentences.en: We all know that.
sentences.zh: 我们大家都知道。

sentences.en: We've known that for years.
sentences.zh: 我们已经知道好几年了。

sentences.en: It's around the time that she receives that diagnosis that Diane starts rearranging her affairs.
sentences.zh: 正是在她确诊的前后，黛安开始重新安排她的事务。

sentences.en: That's when Denzel was added to the bank accounts.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时，丹泽尔被加到了银行账户上。

sentences.en: She gives Denzel her financial power of attorney.
sentences.zh: 她授予了丹泽尔财务委托代理权。

sentences.en: He was a signer.
sentences.zh: 他是签字人。

sentences.en: He could co-sign on mom's checks.
sentences.zh: 他可以在妈妈的支票上共同署名。

sentences.en: She redrafts her will so that if she dies before Denzel, he has the right to live on her property.
sentences.zh: 她重新起草了遗嘱，这样如果她比丹泽尔先去世，他就有权居住在她的房产里。

sentences.en: Basically, it gave Denzel control of almost everything.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这让丹泽尔掌控了几乎一切。

sentences.en: And she also dissolves her financial truSt.
sentences.zh: 她还解散了她的财务信托。

sentences.en: This is the trust that her daughter Julie managed, which holds all of her assets and all of her investments.
sentences.zh: 这就是由她的女儿朱莉管理、持有她所有资产和所有投资的那个信托。

sentences.en: And when Julie checks Diane's bank statements, she starts seeing cash withdrawals of hundreds of dollars at a time.
sentences.zh: 当朱莉查看黛安的银行对账单时，她开始发现每次数百美元的现金提取。

sentences.en: This was especially worrying because they knew that their mother was worth around $4 million and that Denzel, you know, three times divorced, a retired horseshoer,
sentences.zh: 这尤其令人担忧，因为她们知道母亲身家大约有400万美元，而丹泽尔——你知道的，离过三次婚、退休的钉蹄匠——

sentences.en: was worth basically nothing.
sentences.zh: 基本上身无分文。

sentences.en: Denzel had taken mom's phones away.
sentences.zh: 丹泽尔拿走了妈妈的电话。

sentences.en: We couldn't talk to her on the phone.
sentences.zh: 我们在电话里联系不上她。

sentences.en: We didn't know if she was dead or alive.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道她是死是活。

sentences.en: He wouldn't respond to us anymore.
sentences.zh: 他再也不回复我们的消息了。

sentences.en: We were scared.
sentences.zh: 我们很害怕。

sentences.en: All of this just leads Chris and Julie to the conclusion that they need to get to the bottom of what's been happening.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切让克里斯和朱莉得出结论：她们必须查明到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: I was just sitting in the chair in my living room and it's like something swept over me and said, you need to go to Iowa right now.
sentences.zh: 我正坐在客厅的椅子上，就像有什么东西席卷了我，对我说，你现在必须去爱荷华州。

sentences.en: So what do they decide to do?
sentences.zh: 所以她们决定怎么做？

sentences.en: Their first step is to call a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他们的第一步是给律师打电话。

sentences.en: And the lawyer recommended that they obtain what's called a temporary protective order,
sentences.zh: 律师建议她们申请所谓的临时保护令，

sentences.en: basically an emergency restraining order that would force Denzel to move out of the house and stay away from Diane.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是一项紧急限制令，将迫使丹泽尔搬出房子并远离黛安。

sentences.en: And the sisters hoped really give them a chance to sit down with their mother away from Denzel's influence and really get to the bottom of what was happening.
sentences.zh: 姐妹俩希望这能真正给她们一个机会，在远离丹泽尔影响的情况下与母亲坐下来谈谈，真正弄清到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And that's what the restraining order would, in theory, do, right?
sentences.zh: 理论上讲，限制令起到的就是这个作用，对吧？

sentences.en: It wouldn't get Denzel arrested, but it would get him out of the house.
sentences.zh: 它不会让丹泽尔被捕，但能把他赶出房子。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So as a lawyer sort of working away on this paperwork, Chris and Julie get on a flight home to Iowa.
sentences.zh: 因此，当律师在一边忙着处理这些文件时，克里斯和朱莉登上了飞回爱荷华州的航班。

sentences.en: It was, I think, on a Thursday that we flew in to Omaha.
sentences.zh: 我想我们是在一个星期四飞抵奥马哈的。

sentences.en: It's October 2017.
They drive up to the old farmhouse.
sentences.zh: 她们开车来到那栋老旧的农舍前。

sentences.en: Our level of fear driving up that driveway was unreal because we didn't know how Denzel was going to react.
sentences.zh: 沿着车道开上去时，我们心中的恐惧简直无法形容，因为我们不知道丹泽尔会有什么反应。

sentences.en: We didn't know how soon the police were going to be there.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道警察什么时候能到那里。

sentences.en: Walking up to that door was the most frightening moment of my life.
sentences.zh: 走向那扇门是我一生中最恐惧的时刻。

sentences.en: They knock on the side door.
sentences.zh: 她们敲了敲侧门。

sentences.en: They describe their mother answering.
sentences.zh: 她们描述了母亲开门的情形。

sentences.en: And her initial response to them being there is to hesitate.
sentences.zh: 她对她们出现的最初反应是迟疑。

sentences.en: She just stood there and I said, Mom, can we come in?
sentences.zh: 她就站在那儿，我说，妈，我们可以进去吗？

sentences.en: And she goes, oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 然后她说，哦，行啊。

sentences.en: You know, like she was startled.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像她被吓了一跳一样。

sentences.en: Like, of course she can come in.
sentences.zh: 就像，她当然可以进来。

sentences.en: When the daughters walk into the house, they are shocked by what they see.
sentences.zh: 当女儿们走进屋里时，眼前的景象让她们大吃一惊。

sentences.en: This farmhouse, which was once scrupulously tidy, now just looks unkempt.
sentences.zh: 这座曾经一丝不苟、井井有条的农舍，现在看起来却一片凌乱。

sentences.en: In the kitchen, the landline phone is missing and the shelves are basically bare.
sentences.zh: 在厨房里，座机不见了，架子基本上空空如也。

sentences.en: The only food that Diane seems to have in the house is a freezer full of ice cream cones.
sentences.zh: 黛安家里似乎仅有的食物是一个装满冰淇淋甜筒的冰柜。

sentences.en: On the stove, there's this piece of masking tape with Denzel's handwriting on it.
sentences.zh: 在炉灶上，有一条贴着美纹纸胶带的便签，上面是丹泽尔的笔迹。

sentences.en: It says, do not use in big letters.
sentences.zh: 上面用大写字母写着：请勿使用。

sentences.en: On the doorframe, there's this piece of wood that's just blocking access to the staircase.
sentences.zh: 在门框上，有一块木板正挡着通往楼梯的去路。

sentences.en: When we go in, we find our mom incapable of doing anything or understanding why we're there or anything.
sentences.zh: 当我们进去时，我们发现妈妈什么也做不了，也不明白我们为什么会在那里，什么都不懂。

sentences.en: And their mother just seems completely out of it.
sentences.zh: 她们的母亲看起来完全神志不清。

sentences.en: Her curly white hair, which is usually perfectly styled and puffed, is flat around her neck as if it hasn't been washed.
sentences.zh: 她那头通常梳理得完美且蓬松的白色卷发软塌塌地贴在脖子周围，仿佛很久没洗过一样。

sentences.en: Her watch is on upside down.
sentences.zh: 她的手表戴反了。

sentences.en: Her words come out slurred.
sentences.zh: 她说话含糊不清。

sentences.en: Eventually, Diane kind of gives up and goes into the bedroom and just lies face down on her bed.
sentences.zh: 最后，黛安有点放弃了，走进卧室，直接脸朝下趴在床上。

sentences.en: So Chris and I just tried to make conversation, hoping and praying that the police would come driving up the driveway.
sentences.zh: 所以我和克里斯只是试图找话说，心里又期盼又祈祷警察快点把车开进车道。

sentences.en: As expected, for the daughters, two sheriff's deputies pull up.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，两名警长副手为女儿们驱车赶到。

sentences.en: And I looked at Chris like, oh, you know, because I didn't know how he was going to react.
sentences.zh: 我看着克里斯，哦，你知道的，因为我不知道他会有什么反应。

sentences.en: The deputies explained that under the terms of the order, Denzel would be immediately removed from Diane's home and, quote,
sentences.zh: 警员们解释说，根据禁令的条款，丹泽尔将被立即驱逐出黛安的住所，并被引述为：

sentences.en: restrained from committing further acts of abuse or threats of elder abuse, charges that Denzel immediately denied.
sentences.zh: “禁止实施进一步的虐待行为或虐待老人的威胁”——丹泽尔对这些指控立即予以否认。

sentences.en: Chris went straight back to the bedroom so that she could be with mom.
sentences.zh: 克里斯径直回到卧室，这样她就能陪着妈妈。

sentences.en: Because I said, I don't want mom to be upset or to wake up to any of what's going on.
sentences.zh: 因为我说过，我不想让妈妈心烦，也不想让她醒来面对正在发生的一切。

sentences.en: So when the sister's telling, Denzel runs into Diane's bedroom where she's sleeping.
sentences.zh: 因此，当姐妹俩在说话时，丹泽尔冲进了黛安正在睡觉的卧室。

sentences.en: And he's screaming at my mom, Diane, Diane, do you know what those girls have done?
sentences.zh: 他冲着我妈大喊大叫：黛安，黛安，你知道那些丫头都干了些什么吗？

sentences.en: Do you know what they're doing to me?
sentences.zh: 你知道她们对我做了什么吗？

sentences.en: Starts screaming at the top of his lungs.
sentences.zh: 开始歇斯底里地大喊大叫。

sentences.en: It was utter chaos.
sentences.zh: 简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: And then is sort of forced to leave the home.
sentences.zh: 然后他被强行逐出了家门。

sentences.en: The look on his face when he walked out that door was, I wish you were dead.
sentences.zh: 他走出那扇门时的表情就像在说，我巴不得你死掉。

sentences.en: He was furious.
sentences.zh: 他气急败坏。

sentences.en: He was furious.
sentences.zh: 他暴跳如雷。

sentences.en: I don't think Chris and Julie really had plans for what would come next.
sentences.zh: 我想克里斯和朱莉并没有为接下来会发生什么做真正长远的打算。

sentences.en: And I think what surprised them most on that initial day was that none of this seemed to register for Diane at all.
sentences.zh: 而且我想，最她们感到意外的是，在最初的那天，黛安对这一切似乎毫无感知。

sentences.en: You know, when the police left, she fell asleep.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，警察离开后，她就睡着了。

sentences.en: The first thing she said when she woke up from her nap, despite having witnessed, you know, this whole scene before her was, where's Denzel?
sentences.zh: 尽管刚刚目睹了眼前发生的这一切，她从午睡中醒来后说的第一句话却是：丹泽尔呢？

sentences.en: And she asked it again, and she asked it again, and all evening, and in the middle of the night, and the next day, too.
sentences.zh: 她一遍又一遍地问，整个晚上、半夜以及第二天都在问。

sentences.en: She didn't even know where he had gone.
sentences.zh: 她甚至不知道他去了哪里。

sentences.en: And I think the daughters, you know, they tried to explain to their mother what was happening.
sentences.zh: 我想女儿们，你知道的，她们试着向母亲解释发生了什么。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Can I ask a question?
sentences.zh: 我能问个问题吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, but you don't necessarily get an answer.
sentences.zh: 可以，但不一定能得到答案。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Later, I listened to this long conversation that Chris recorded on her phone.
sentences.zh: 后来，我听了克里斯用手机录下的这段长长的对话。

sentences.en: Did you terminate my general power of attorney?
sentences.zh: 你终止了我的全面委托代理权吗？

sentences.en: And you can hear Chris and Julie, you know, ask questions of their mother.
sentences.zh: 你能听到克里斯和朱莉，你知道的，在向她们的母亲提出问题。

sentences.en: What do you mean general power of attorney?
sentences.zh: 你说的全面委托代理权是什么意思？

sentences.en: Just, I had a, I know you terminated my trust, but did you also terminate my power of attorney?
sentences.zh: 就是，我有一个——我知道你终止了我的信托，但你也终止了我的委托代理权吗？

sentences.en: What is the power of, not to my knowledge, what?
sentences.zh: 什么委不委托的，我不知道，什么？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: And Diane's responses are really shocking.
sentences.zh: 而黛安的回答实在令人震惊。

sentences.en: She says, you know, what's the power of attorney?
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道的，什么是委托代理权？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And there are changes she doesn't remember making.
sentences.zh: 有些她做过的改变，她已经记不清了。

sentences.en: You know, I could grasp nothing about the truSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，关于那个信托，我什么也记不起来了。

sentences.en: All I know is it was there, and you doled it up.
sentences.zh: 我只知道它在那儿，然后你把它分掉了。

sentences.en: I never doled anything from your 12th.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有分过你12号的任何东西。

sentences.en: She's using that.
sentences.zh: 她在用那个词。

sentences.en: But while Diane clearly doesn't understand, you know, the precise financial and legal decisions that she made, her motivation is very clear.
sentences.zh: 然而，虽然黛安显然并不理解她做出的那些具体的财务和法律决定，但她的动机却非常明确。

sentences.en: A long time ago, after Dad died, we did this.
sentences.zh: 很久以前，爸爸去世后，我们做了这件事。

sentences.en: You asked me, you said, Mom, you know, do you want to take care of their trust?
sentences.zh: 你问过我，你说，妈，你知道的，你想接管那个信托吗？

sentences.en: And I looked at you and I said, honey, I don't know if I know the first thing about that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 我看着你，我说，亲爱的，我不知道我对这种事情是不是一窍不通。

sentences.en: Do you want to do it?
sentences.zh: 你想做吗？

sentences.en: And you said, I'd be happy to.
sentences.zh: 你说，我很乐意效劳。

sentences.en: And I said, okay, go ahead.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，那就去做吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: She tells her daughters, I want to make my own decisions.
sentences.zh: 她告诉她的女儿们，我想自己做决定。

sentences.en: I want to be in charge of myself until I die.
sentences.zh: 在我去世之前，我想自己当家作主。

sentences.en: I knew that I had given you control of it for me because back before, because I didn't have a clue and my mind wasn't working very well anyway.
sentences.zh: 我知道我以前把它的控制权交给你是因为过去，因为我一无所知，而且反正我的脑子也不太好使了。

sentences.en: Probably better than it is now.
sentences.zh: 可能比现在好点有限。

sentences.en: But I want to be my own person.
sentences.zh: 但我想要做回真正的自己。

sentences.en: I'm realizing, Katie, in this moment that I don't really understand what the law has to say about this complicated situation.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，此时此刻我意识到，对于法律如何看待这种复杂的情况，我其实并不是很懂。

sentences.en: I mean, here, Diane is asking to see Denzel, who has just been removed from the House per that protective order.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这里，黛安要求见丹泽尔，而丹泽尔刚刚根据那项保护令被带离了住宅。

sentences.en: And Diane is taking actions like giving him power of attorney, but she's been given a diagnosis of dementia.
sentences.zh: 而且黛安还采取了授予他委托书之类的行动，但她已经被诊断出患有痴呆症。

sentences.en: And that recording you heard suggests she doesn't even understand what power of attorney is at this moment,
sentences.zh: 你刚才听到的那段录音表明，她此刻甚至不明白什么是委托书，

sentences.en: both of which runs contrary to the idea that she's really capable of being in control of her life and these kinds of decisions.
sentences.zh: 这两点都与她真正有能力掌控自己的人生和这类决定的看法相悖。

sentences.en: So what does the law say about that?
sentences.zh: 那么，法律对此是怎么说的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, this definitely confused Diane's daughter, and it confuses a lot of adult children, of people with dementia.
sentences.zh: 是的，这绝对让黛安的女儿感到困惑，这也让许多患有痴呆症患者的成年子女感到困惑。

sentences.en: Adult children often assume that, you know, the moment a doctor pronounces a person to have dementia, that kind of flips a decisional switch.
sentences.zh: 成年子女通常会认为，你知道的，就在医生宣布一个人患有痴呆症的那一刻，这就好像按下了决定能力的开关。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, that person is now legally and medically incapable of choosing for herself anymore.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，这个人从法律和医学上讲，再也没有能力为自己做选择 了。

sentences.en: The reality is that there's no such switch within modern medicine.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，现代医学中根本没有这样的开关。

sentences.en: Patients are never declared completely competent or incompetent in some holistic sense.
sentences.zh: 从某种整体意义上讲，患者绝不会被宣布为完全具备行为能力或完全不具备行为能力。

sentences.en: Instead, doctors are asked to look at individual choices and whether or not a person is able to make a specific choice in a specific moment.
sentences.zh: 相反，医生被要求考察具体的选择，以及一个人是否能够在特定的时刻做出特定的选择。

sentences.en: This, in practice, can mean that a person with dementia can retain the ability to make choices for many years and then lose the ability in stages.
sentences.zh: 这在实践中意味着，患有痴呆症的人可以保留多年的做选择的能力，然后分阶段失去这种能力。

sentences.en: So lose the ability to make complex choices first and then simple ones later.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，先失去做出复杂选择的能力，然后再失去简单选择的能力。

sentences.en: And this is important from a legal perspective, too, because it means that people with dementia retain the ability to make legal choices even when they are cognitively impaired.
sentences.zh: 从法律的角度来看，这一点也很重要，因为这意味着痴呆症患者即使在认知受损的情况下，仍然保留着做出法律选择的能力。

sentences.en: But of course, this often creates conflicts within families because there's no clear-cut medical way to determine, without error,
sentences.zh: 但当然，这经常在家庭内部产生冲突，因为没有一种清晰的、万无一失的医学方法来确定，

sentences.en: that a person is capable of making a specific choice.
sentences.zh: 一个人是否有能力做出特定的选择。

sentences.en: So based on what you just said, the daughter's options would seem to be pretty limited here.
sentences.zh: 所以根据你刚才所说，女儿们的选择在这里似乎相当有限。

sentences.en: So what is their next move?
sentences.zh: 那么她们的下一步行动是什么？

sentences.en: It's clear to Chris and Julie that their mother had been very effective at hiding the extent of her impairment from them.
sentences.zh: 克里斯和朱莉很清楚，她们的母亲在向她们隐瞒病情严重程度这方面非常有一套。

sentences.en: At this point, Diana's still speaking well and she can be engaged in conversation.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，黛安说话仍然很流利，并且能够参与对话。

sentences.en: So her daughters decide that it's probably going to be important for them to get some evidence that their mother is actually very sick.
sentences.zh: 因此，她的女儿们认为，她们去收集一些母亲确实病得很重的证据，可能非常重要。

sentences.en: And their decision is to bring her to the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinic,
sentences.zh: 她们的决定是带她去爱荷华大学医院和诊所，

sentences.en: where they know there's a dedicated geriatric psychiatry unit where their mother can get a more formal assessment.
sentences.zh: 她们知道那里有一个专门的老年精神病学病房，母亲可以在那里接受更正式的评估。

sentences.en: And so we sat mom down and explained it to her as best we could without having it sound scary, like we're taking you to a hospital.
sentences.zh: 于是我们让妈妈坐下，尽可能不让她感到害怕、不像是在带她去医院那样向她解释了这件事。

sentences.en: And they're telling Diana agrees to go.
sentences.zh: 她们说黛安同意去了。

sentences.en: She helps to pack her bag.
sentences.zh: 她帮着收拾自己的包。

sentences.en: She gets into the car.
sentences.zh: 她上了车。

sentences.en: And they all start in on this hours-long drive to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 他们一行人开始驱车数小时前往医院。

sentences.en: Everything stayed quiet in the car for quite a while.
sentences.zh: 在车里，一切安静了相当长一段时间。

sentences.en: We got to Des Moines and my phone rang and it was our attorney's mother, who's a nurse.
sentences.zh: 我们到了得梅因，我的电话响了，打来的是我们律师的母亲，她是一名护士。

sentences.en: It's sometime around sunset.
sentences.zh: 时间大约在日落时分。

sentences.en: And mom said, who is that?
sentences.zh: 妈妈问，那是谁？

sentences.en: I said, Eileen.
sentences.zh: 我说，是艾琳。

sentences.en: Well, can I talk to her?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我能和她说话吗？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: That Diane starts getting upset.
sentences.zh: 黛安开始变得情绪激动。

sentences.en: So she gets the phone.
sentences.zh: 于是她接了电话。

sentences.en: Eileen, I'm being kidnapped.
sentences.zh: 艾琳，我被绑架了。

sentences.en: Please call the police.
sentences.zh: 请报警。

sentences.en: Come and get me.
sentences.zh: 来接我。

sentences.en: I'm being kidnapped.
sentences.zh: 我被绑架了。

sentences.en: And Eileen.
sentences.zh: 还有艾琳。

sentences.en: At some point, she throws a book at Julie.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，她朝朱莉扔了一本书。

sentences.en: She starts hitting Chris.
sentences.zh: 她开始打克里斯。

sentences.en: And I had to grab her wrist to keep her from continuing to hit me.
sentences.zh: 我不得不抓住她的手腕，防止她继续打我。

sentences.en: She's screaming that she doesn't know where she is and is being, you know, driven somewhere against her will.
sentences.zh: 她尖叫着说她不知道自己在哪里，而且你知道的，她是在违背自己意愿的情况下被载往某处的。

sentences.en: Yes, it was terrifying.
sentences.zh: 是的，这太吓人了。

sentences.en: Physically, it's the voice.
sentences.zh: 从身体上来说，那是声音。

sentences.en: It's the body.
sentences.zh: 那是身体。

sentences.en: It's everything that nurtured you before.
sentences.zh: 那是以前滋养过你的一切。

sentences.en: And suddenly, it's like she's possessed.
sentences.zh: 而突然之间，她就像是被附身了一样。

sentences.en: After a few minutes of this, the sisters decide they're going to call an ambulance and have an ambulance drive Diane the rest of the way to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 经历了这几分钟的混乱后，姐妹俩决定叫一辆救护车，让救护车把黛安送到医院剩下的路程。

sentences.en: When they get there, Diane's given a cognitive assessment.
sentences.zh: 当她们到达那里时，黛安接受了认知评估。

sentences.en: And what's shocking is that, you know, while Diane has been operating more or less normally in her life, she actually has very significant deficits.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊的是，你知道的，虽然黛安在生活中或多或少一直像正常人一样行动，但她实际上有非常严重的认知缺陷。

sentences.en: The neuropsychologist who tests her describes deficits in almost every field that he tests for and decides that Diane is unable to safely perform tasks as complex as preparing a meal.
sentences.zh: 对她进行测试的神经心理学家描述说，她在所测试的几乎每个领域都存在缺陷，并认为黛安无法安全地完成准备饭菜这样复杂的任务。

sentences.en: In his final report, he describes Diane as having significantly limited capacity for informed personal, medical, and financial decision-making.
sentences.zh: 在他的最终报告中，他描述黛安在做出明智的个人、医疗和财务决策方面的能力受到严重限制。

sentences.en: Later, a doctor helps to kind of interpret these findings and she uses the phrase Alzheimer's disease for the first time.
sentences.zh: 后来，一位医生协助解读了这些发现，她首次使用了阿尔茨海默病这个词。

sentences.en: In her view, Diane is already at a late moderate stage, so far beyond the kind of mild forgetfulness that had started to worry her daughters.
sentences.zh: 在她看来，黛安已经处于中度晚期，远远超出了那种曾让女儿们开始感到担忧的轻度健忘。

sentences.en: So the kids wanted to know how bad things had gotten for their mom, and now they know.
sentences.zh: 所以孩子们曾经想知道她们的母亲情况有多糟，现在她们知道了。

sentences.en: I mean, they have a very serious diagnosis now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她们现在得到了一个非常严重的诊断。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that really convinces them that they need to take control of the situation in a more formal way.
sentences.zh: 这确实说服了她们，让她们觉得需要以一种更正式的方式来掌控局面。

sentences.en: So talking to their lawyer, Chris and Julie decide that they're going to focus on getting legal guardianship of their mother,
sentences.zh: 因此，在与她们的律师交谈后，克里斯和朱莉决定专注于获得对母亲的法定监护权，

sentences.en: which will effectively give them control over many of her personal and medical choices.
sentences.zh: 这将有效地使她们能够控制她的许多个人和医疗选择。

sentences.en: And they're convinced that, you know, this will be a fairly straightforward case, and that once they get guardianship, they'll be able to kind of fix everything.
sentences.zh: 并且她们深信，你知道的，这将是一个相当直接的案件，一旦她们获得了监护权，她们就能把一切都修好。

sentences.en: But it's also at this point that their personal relationship with their mother really evaporates.
sentences.zh: 但也是在这个时候，她们与母亲的个人关系真正破裂了。

sentences.en: Diane is moved from the hospital to an assisted living facility in Denison, and because the elder abuse charges against Denzel have been dropped,
sentences.zh: 黛安从医院搬到了丹尼森的一家辅助生活机构，由于针对丹泽尔虐待老人的指控已被撤销，

sentences.en: she's able to start seeing him again.
sentences.zh: 她得以重新开始见他。

sentences.en: And once that happens, Diane quickly makes the choice to stop seeing her children.
sentences.zh: 一旦这种情况发生，黛安很快就做出了不再见自己孩子的选择。

sentences.en: She tells pretty much everyone she knows, everyone she sees, that she wants nothing to do with them, that she doesn't want them to visit.
sentences.zh: 她几乎对她认识的每一个人、见到的每一个人都说，她不想和她们有任何瓜葛，她不希望她们来探望。

sentences.en: At one point, she even tells a friend she doesn't have daughters anymore.
sentences.zh: 有一回，她甚至对一个朋友说她再也没有女儿了。

sentences.en: Yeah, hello.
sentences.zh: 喂，你好。

sentences.en: Hi, Denzel.
sentences.zh: 嗨，丹泽尔。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: There's this recording of a phone call.
sentences.zh: 这里有一段电话录音。

sentences.en: I'm not sure where to start, so I'll tell you what I planned on saying, and that is that I would be happy to sit down and talk with you and Nana.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该从哪里开始，所以我就说说我原本打算说的话，那就是我很高兴能坐下来，和你们以及奶奶谈谈。

sentences.en: Well, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: I'll have to get back to you.
sentences.zh: 我得回复你。

sentences.en: Please let me tell my grandmother the same thing.
sentences.zh: 请允许我也把同样的话转告我的外祖母。

sentences.en: I'll let you tell her.
sentences.zh: 我让你告诉她。

sentences.en: Julie's daughter, Haley, calls her grandmother, Diane, and tries to mediate the situation.
sentences.zh: 朱莉的女儿海莉给外祖母黛安打电话，试图调解这种情况。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 喂。

sentences.en: Hi, Nana.
sentences.zh: 嗨，奶奶。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Over the course of the call, you really hear Haley try to make the case that...
sentences.zh: 在通话过程中，你真的能听到海莉试图表达……

sentences.en: I love all of my family.
sentences.zh: 我爱我所有的家人。

sentences.en: I love you both.
sentences.zh: 我爱你们俩。

sentences.en: I love my mother and aunt.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的母亲和阿姨。

sentences.en: You know, this has just got out of control.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，事情已经失控了。

sentences.en: Chris and Julie love their mother.
sentences.zh: 克里斯和朱莉爱她们的母亲。

sentences.en: I need you both to know, and I need especially Denzel to know, that from my perspective, there are opportunities for everybody to come together and everybody to be happy,
sentences.zh: 我需要你们两个都知道，我尤其需要丹泽尔知道，从我的角度来看，大家有机会重新聚在一起，每个人都能获得幸福，

sentences.en: especially Nana.
sentences.zh: 尤其是奶奶。

sentences.en: And there's got to be some way to resolve this.
sentences.zh: 肯定有某种方法可以解决这个问候。

sentences.en: It's up to Nana whether she accepts them again.
sentences.zh: 这取决于奶奶是否再次接受她们。

sentences.en: Not them and Nana.
sentences.zh: 不是她们和奶奶。

sentences.en: It's up to Nana.
sentences.zh: 这取决于奶奶。

sentences.en: And she has chosen to write them all.
sentences.zh: 而她已经选择不再理会他们所有人。

sentences.en: I have chosen to write them all, she has.
sentences.zh: 我已经选择不再理会他们所有人，她是的。

sentences.en: And Diane, for her part, she speaks very lucidly.
sentences.zh: 而黛安就她个人而言，说话非常清晰连贯。

sentences.en: I know there's an easy way out of this, and there is not.
sentences.zh: 我知道这里有一条摆脱困境的捷径，但根本没有。

sentences.en: I can't handle much more.
sentences.zh: 我承受不了更多了。

sentences.en: And the only way I can get rid of that stress is to get rid of what's causing the stress, which happens to me.
sentences.zh: 我摆脱这种压力的唯一方法，就是摆脱导致压力的事情，而这正好落在我身上。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉。

sentences.en: She says quite clearly, there's not a way to move on.
sentences.zh: 她非常清楚地表明，根本没有继续前进的办法。

sentences.en: It's going to save my life, and it's the only thing I can do for you, and I have to accept it.
sentences.zh: 这将拯救我的生命，这是我能为你做的唯一一件事，我必须接受它。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉。

sentences.en: Don't be back, Haley.
sentences.zh: 海莉，不要再回来了。

sentences.en: I want you to know I love you.
sentences.zh: 我想让你知道我爱你。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 深空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想要看看下一颗恒星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代冰淇淋。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都使用不同的起始单词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅端食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175周年，陪伴您理解世界，充分过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受nytimes.com slash subscribe上的特惠活动。

sentences.en: Hi, Mr. Nelson.
sentences.zh: 嗨，纳尔逊先生。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for getting back to me again.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你再次给我回电话。

sentences.en: Can you hear me okay?
sentences.zh: 你能听清我说话吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Okay, great.
sentences.zh: 好的，太好了。

sentences.en: And thanks for those people.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你提供的那些人。

sentences.en: So Katie, you eventually spoke with Denzel about how he saw his relationship with Diane and with her family.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，你后来和丹泽尔谈过，关于他是如何看待自己与黛安以及她家人的关系的。

sentences.en: So in his mind, how did all of this play out?
sentences.zh: 那么在他看来，这一切是怎么发展到这一步的？

sentences.en: So Denzel also describes falling in love as sort of sudden and unexpected.
sentences.zh: 所以丹泽尔也形容坠入爱河是某种突然而又意料之外的事。

sentences.en: Well, one day I decided I was just going to go for a drive.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一天我决定我只是要去兜风。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And Diane was out working in the yard and she says, well, what are you up to today?
sentences.zh: 黛安当时正在院子里干活，她说，嗯，你今天打算做什么？

sentences.en: And I said, you know, it's a nice day.
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道的，今天天气很好。

sentences.en: And I'm going to get in the truck and just go for a drive.
sentences.zh: 我要上卡车去兜风。

sentences.en: When I first got in touch with him on the phone, he told me this long story about falling in love with Diane and his truck.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次在电话里与他取得联系时，他给我讲了这么一个长篇故事，关于他和黛安以及他的卡车坠入爱河的经历。

sentences.en: I said, you want to come along?
sentences.zh: 我说，你想一起去吗？

sentences.en: And she said, well, where are you going?
sentences.zh: 她说，嗯，你要去哪儿？

sentences.en: I said, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我说，我不知道。

sentences.en: She said, well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 她说，好吧，行。

sentences.en: And that day they took their first drive.
sentences.zh: 那天他们进行了第一次兜风。

sentences.en: Soon one drive became regular drives and then longer drives.
sentences.zh: 很快，一次兜风变成了例行的兜风，接着是更长时间的兜风。

sentences.en: They took trips to horse shows and quilt shows and antique sales all around the state.
sentences.zh: 他们去参观了全州各地的马展、拼布展和古董展销会。

sentences.en: One of the first trips we made, it always tickled me because her husband was an attorney.
sentences.zh: 我们进行的最早的几次旅行之一，总是让我觉得很有趣，因为她的丈夫是一名律师。

sentences.en: And every trip they ever went on, they had to be certain such a place because they had a motel.
sentences.zh: 而且他们每次出门旅行，都必须确保有那样的地方，因为他们要住汽车旅馆。

sentences.en: You know, these trips were themselves kind of an entirely new experience for Diane.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对黛安来说，这些旅行本身就是一种全新而特别的体验。

sentences.en: And the first trip we went on, we just took off.
sentences.zh: 我们去的第一趟旅行，说走就走。

sentences.en: She says, where are we staying tonight?
sentences.zh: 她说，我们今晚住哪儿？

sentences.en: And I said, well, where do you want to stay?
sentences.zh: 我说，你想住哪儿？

sentences.en: Diane, he said, was amazed to learn that Denzel never booked a motel room in advance.
sentences.zh: 他说，黛安得知丹泽从来不提前预订汽车旅馆房间时，感到十分惊讶。

sentences.en: He just got in his car and drove and drove until he felt like stopping.
sentences.zh: 他只是上车，一直开，一直开，直到想停下来为止。

sentences.en: And then he'd stay at whatever motel happened to have space.
sentences.zh: 然后他就会住在刚好有空房的任意一家汽车旅馆里。

sentences.en: So she liked how it was kind of more spontaneous traveling with you.
sentences.zh: 所以她很喜欢这种和你在一起更具随性色彩的旅行方式。

sentences.en: The spontaneous deal was something that just really tickled her.
sentences.zh: 这种说走就走的旅行方式让她感到无比开心。

sentences.en: And Denzel says that on those longer trips, they would sometimes stay overnight at a motel.
sentences.zh: 丹泽说，在那些较长的旅途中，他们有时会在汽车旅馆过夜。

sentences.en: In the beginning, of course, they're just friends.
sentences.zh: 一开始，他们当然只是普通朋友。

sentences.en: So they would sleep in two separate beds.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会睡在两张不同的床上。

sentences.en: He talked about leaving the room to go outside while she got dressed.
sentences.zh: 他谈到她穿衣服时，他会离开房间去外面。

sentences.en: And he'd do the same for her.
sentences.zh: 他也会为她这样做。

sentences.en: But then one night, as he told it, Diane just climbed out of her bed and into his arMs.
sentences.zh: 但据他讲述，后来有一天晚上，黛安直接从自己的床上爬到了他的怀里。

sentences.en: And he thought at that moment about how she was the gentlest person he'd ever met.
sentences.zh: 那一刻他觉得，她是自己见过的最温柔的人。

sentences.en: Finally, one day, we ended up in a big house.
sentences.zh: 最后有一天，我们来到了一栋大房子里。

sentences.en: And I was invited.
sentences.zh: 我也被邀请了。

sentences.en: And so this relationship just blossoMs.
sentences.zh: 于是这段感情就这么蓬勃发展起来。

sentences.en: It was, we had some really, a couple, three really good years there from, oh, 2013 until this all made the fan.
sentences.zh: 那段日子，我们在那儿度过了相当不错的一段时光，从大约2013年一直到这一切闹得沸沸扬扬。

sentences.en: When Denzel moved in, you know, he knew that Diane's daughters weren't really accepting of the relationship.
sentences.zh: 丹泽搬进去的时候，你知道的，他知道黛安的女儿们其实并不接受这段关系。

sentences.en: Chris never did like the idea that I was living in her dad's house.
sentences.zh: 克里斯一直不喜欢我住在他爸爸的房子里。

sentences.en: But he also didn't really care.
sentences.zh: 但他其实也无所谓。

sentences.en: You know, it wasn't her dad's house anymore.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那已经不再是她爸爸的房子了。

sentences.en: It was her mother's house.
sentences.zh: 那是她妈妈的房子。

sentences.en: I think Denzel felt like, you know, Diane was a grown woman and she was entitled to make her own decisions.
sentences.zh: 我想丹泽觉得，黛安是个成年女性，她有权做出自己的决定。

sentences.en: And it didn't really bother him whether a couple of daughters who lived out of state approved of him or not.
sentences.zh: 至于几个住在外州的女儿是否认可他，他其实并不在意。

sentences.en: But later, I think Denzel started to butt heads more with Chris and Julie.
sentences.zh: 但后来，我想丹泽开始与克里斯和朱莉产生更多冲突。

sentences.en: It seemed to him that Diane's daughters were interested in controlling things for their mother.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，黛安的女儿们似乎一心想掌控她们母亲的一切。

sentences.en: You know, he was surprised to learn that even Diane's social security check went straight into an account that was managed by Julie.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他惊讶地发现，就连黛安的社保支票也直接打入了由朱莉管理的账户。

sentences.en: And he described being sort of disturbed to learn that whenever Diane wanted to do anything major, like trade in her car for one she liked better, she had to go through Julie,
sentences.zh: 他描述说，每当黛安想做点什么大事，比如换一辆她更喜欢的车时，都必须通过朱莉，这让他感到有些不安，

sentences.en: who was the trustee of her truSt.
sentences.zh: 朱莉是她信托基金的受托人。

sentences.en: Did it bother her that Julie was kind of in charge of things or did she like it because it was easier?
sentences.zh: 朱莉大权在握这件事让她觉得困扰，还是因为这样更省事而让她乐见其成？

sentences.en: No, she hated it.
sentences.zh: 不，她恨透了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: She was perfectly able to take care of her own bills and everything.
sentences.zh: 她完全有能力自己处理账单和各种事务。

sentences.en: I'm curious what Denzel's interpretation and recollection is of the day that Diane's daughters show up with that order forcing him to leave the house.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道，对于黛安的女儿们拿着强制他离开房屋的命令出现的那天，丹泽是怎么解释和回忆的。

sentences.en: I think he was completely amazed by it.
sentences.zh: 我想他对此完全感到震惊。

sentences.en: I was home and I saw Chris and Julie come up to the door and I told Diane, I says, there's going to be trouble.
sentences.zh: 我在家里看到克里斯和朱莉走到门口，我告诉黛安，我说，要有麻烦了。

sentences.en: He didn't see it coming at all.
sentences.zh: 他完全没有预料到这一点。

sentences.en: And then the sheriff showed up and they had a restraining order and they hauled me out of the house.
sentences.zh: 然后治安官就出现了，他们拿着限制令，把我强行拖出了房子。

sentences.en: And I heard Chris tell Diane, Denzel did something illegal and you're never going to see it again.
sentences.zh: 我听见克里斯对黛安说，丹泽做了违法的事，你再也见不到他了。

sentences.en: In Denzel's version of events, he doesn't resist at all.
sentences.zh: 在丹泽版本的经历中，他完全没有反抗。

sentences.en: He goes into Diane's bedroom to say goodbye to her.
sentences.zh: 他走进黛安的卧室去和她道别。

sentences.en: I told Diane, I said, be tough, honey.
sentences.zh: 我告诉黛安，我说，坚强点，亲爱的。

sentences.en: He gathers his various medications and gets into his car and drives away.
sentences.zh: 他收拾好自己的各种药物，上了车，开车离去。

sentences.en: And I think Denzel was completely taken aback when he heard the specific charges that he was accused of.
sentences.zh: 我想，当丹泽听到自己被指控的具体罪名时，完全被吓了一跳。

sentences.en: They charged me with elderly abuse, just one lie right after another.
sentences.zh: 他们指控我虐待老人，全都是一个接一个的谎言。

sentences.en: Certainly, the phrase elder abuse struck him as being entirely inappropriate.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，“虐待老人”这个词让他觉得极其不恰当。

sentences.en: Denzel ended up giving me a copy of his diary from that time and he called them the Sin Sisters,
sentences.zh: 丹泽最后给了我一份他当时写的日记复印件，他把她们称为“罪恶姐妹”，

sentences.en: kind of coming in and making up stories about him hurting this person who he loved more than anyone else.
sentences.zh: 她们跑来捏造各种故事，说他伤害了他最深爱的人。

sentences.en: They said, I wasn't seeing it right or we weren't eating right.
sentences.zh: 她们说，我没有照顾好她，或者我们吃得不对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's the lies they told, you know.
sentences.zh: 那是她们撒的谎，你知道的。

sentences.en: And he had his own explanation for things.
sentences.zh: 而他对种种事情有自己的解释。

sentences.en: Most of the time we went out to eat because we cooked.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数时候都出去吃，因为我们自己做饭。

sentences.en: And Diane had cooked all her lies.
sentences.zh: 而且黛安一辈子都在做饭。

sentences.en: As for the cupboards being bare, well, Denzel said the cupboards were bare because he knew that Diane had spent 50 years of her life cooking for other people.
sentences.zh: 至于橱柜空空如也，丹泽说橱柜空着是因为他知道黛安用50年的生命为别人做饭。

sentences.en: And he thought it would be nice for her to be taken care of.
sentences.zh: 他觉得现在该轮到她被人照顾了，这样挺好的。

sentences.en: They said there was some mold in there and there was no mold.
sentences.zh: 她们说里面有些发霉，根本就没有发霉。

sentences.en: As for the house being dirty, again, he said it looked okay to him.
sentences.zh: 至于房子很脏，他又说，在他看来这挺正常的。

sentences.en: But anyway, he didn't like to see Diane on her hands and knees scrubbing the floor.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，他不愿意看到黛安双膝跪地擦洗地板。

sentences.en: And anytime he did, he told her to get up and not worry about it.
sentences.zh: 只要看到她这样，他就会叫她起来，别担心。

sentences.en: He would take care of things.
sentences.zh: 他会把事情处理好的。

sentences.en: So Denzel, you know, he left the house as he was forced to do.
sentences.zh: 所以丹泽，你知道的，他被迫离开了房子。

sentences.en: But I think from that moment, he had every intention to fight Diane's daughters for what he saw as Diane's freedom and liberation.
sentences.zh: 但我认为从那一刻起，他下定决心要为了他所理解的黛安的自由和解放，与黛安的女儿们抗争到底。

sentences.en: What about the decline of her memory, which, of course, is at the heart of all the legal maneuvers that his daughters are undertaking?
sentences.zh: 那关于她记忆力的衰退呢？这当然是女儿们采取所有法律行动的核心所在。

sentences.en: What does he say about that?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么说的？

sentences.en: He really denies that at this time Diane was sick?
sentences.zh: 他真的否认当时黛安生病了吗？

sentences.en: No, he was not having any memory issues.
sentences.zh: 不，她没有出现任何记忆问题。

sentences.en: So in your opinion, she didn't really have dementia right when this all started?
sentences.zh: 所以依你之见，这一切刚开始的时候她并没有真正患上痴呆症？

sentences.en: She got it later?
sentences.zh: 她是后来才得的吗？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: He noticed Diane was a little less steady on her feet.
sentences.zh: 他注意到黛安走路稍微有点不太稳。

sentences.en: And, you know, maybe her memory wasn't what it was at the age of 30 or 40.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，也许她的记忆力确实不如三四十岁的时候。

sentences.en: But he didn't see it as being some big serious thing.
sentences.zh: 但他并不认为这是一件多么严重的大事。

sentences.en: A lot of people have a bit of dementia.
sentences.zh: 很多人都有点轻度痴呆。

sentences.en: And I think his view was that Diane was more or less unchanged and certainly not changed to the point where she needed someone to be caring for her all of the time.
sentences.zh: 我想他的看法是，黛安基本上没什么变化，当然也没有严重到需要别人全天候照顾她的地步。

sentences.en: He was prepared to care for her in whatever way he said she needed.
sentences.zh: 无论她需要什么样的照顾，他都准备好随时提供。

sentences.en: So what does Denzel do after he and Diane are forcibly separated?
sentences.zh: 那么，在与黛安被迫分开后，丹泽做了什么？

sentences.en: So the first thing he does is leave the house, as he's ordered to do.
sentences.zh: 他做的第一件事就是按照命令离开房子。

sentences.en: He moves in with his son.
sentences.zh: 他搬去和儿子同住。

sentences.en: I just, well, I could have went nuts.
sentences.zh: 我当时，简直快要疯了。

sentences.en: I mean, couldn't connect with her, couldn't call her or nothing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，联系不上她，不能给她打电话，什么都做不了。

sentences.en: But once Diane's transferred to the assisted living facility, he's given visitation rights again and he starts visiting her every day.
sentences.zh: 但一旦黛安被转移到辅助生活机构，他又恢复了探视权，并开始每天去看望她。

sentences.en: Most morning, I'm an early riser.
sentences.zh: 大多数早晨，我起得很早。

sentences.en: I always have been.
sentences.zh: 我一直都是这样。

sentences.en: I wake up at 4 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 我4点钟就醒了。

sentences.en: I don't care what time I go to bed.
sentences.zh: 我才不管几点睡觉。

sentences.en: And so I'd wait around until 7 when I could go out there and go to breakfast with her.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是等到7点钟，然后去那里跟她一起吃早餐。

sentences.en: He shows up at 7 a.m.
sentences.zh: 他早上7点准时出现。

sentences.en: He stays 12 hours.
sentences.zh: 一呆就是12个小时。

sentences.en: He goes for little walks with her around the building.
sentences.zh: 他和她一起在楼里散散步。

sentences.en: He calculates that if they walk around the building 10 times, it's a mile.
sentences.zh: 他计算过，如果绕着大楼走10圈，刚好是一英里。

sentences.en: They'll walk it twice.
sentences.zh: 他们会走上两圈。

sentences.en: He sits with her while she naps.
sentences.zh: 她睡午觉时，他就坐在旁边陪着。

sentences.en: And he says that oftentimes in the night, he would get a call from the assisted living facility and a nurse would tell him that Diane was crying.
sentences.zh: 他说很多时候在夜里，他会接到辅助生活机构的电话，护士会告诉他黛安在哭。

sentences.en: 2 a.m., 3 a.m., that she was crying and she wouldn't stop.
sentences.zh: 凌晨2点，3点，她在哭，而且停不下来。

sentences.en: And they'd ask if he could come.
sentences.zh: 他们会问他能不能过来。

sentences.en: But many nights they'd call me that Diane was having a bad time.
sentences.zh: 但很多天里他们打电话来都是说黛安情况不太好。

sentences.en: What was she?
sentences.zh: 她怎么了？

sentences.en: Was it just because she was sick or she was lonely, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得是因为她生病了还是因为孤独？

sentences.en: She just was what her daughters did to her.
sentences.zh: 她只是在为她女儿对她做的事难过。

sentences.en: And then maybe they tried to call that day or something and she wouldn't talk to them and then she'd be thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 然后可能她们那天尝试打过电话什么的，但她不肯跟她们说话，接着她就会一直琢磨这事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: How would you settle her down?
sentences.zh: 你通常怎么安抚她？

sentences.en: Hug her.
sentences.zh: 抱抱她。

sentences.en: Kiss her.
sentences.zh: 亲亲她。

sentences.en: Tell her everything was going to be all right.
sentences.zh: 告诉她一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: And as Denzel tells it, you know, Diane is very clear throughout this whole time that she loves him, that she wants to be with him, and that more than that,
sentences.zh: 正如丹泽所说，你知道的，黛安在这整个过程中非常明确地表达她爱他，她想和他在一起，不仅如此，

sentences.en: she doesn't want to see her daughters anymore.
sentences.zh: 她再也不想见到她的女儿们了。

sentences.en: And Denzel sees it for himself, he says, you know, when Chris and Julie call, Diane's asked if she wants to take the call, she always says no.
sentences.zh: 丹泽亲眼看到了这一点，他说，你知道的，当克里斯和朱莉打来电话时，问黛安要不要接，她总是说不。

sentences.en: As Christmas approaches, Diane sends word to her daughters through her lawyers that she doesn't want to see them at all.
sentences.zh: 随着圣诞节临近，黛安通过律师向女儿们传话，说她根本不想见她们。

sentences.en: And I think Denzel really feels, heading into the guardianship case, that he has a really good chance of winning because, isn't it obvious,
sentences.zh: 我想丹泽在进入监护权诉讼案时，真的觉得自己有很大的胜算，因为不是很明显吗，

sentences.en: Diane is telling everyone that she wants Denzel and shouldn't it be her choice?
sentences.zh: 黛安在对每个人说她想要丹泽，这难道不应该由她自己选择吗？

sentences.en: Well, eventually a court had to make that decision.
sentences.zh: 好吧，最终法院不得不做出裁决。

sentences.en: Tell us what happened during this trial over guardianship for Diane.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲审理黛安监护权案期间发生了什么。

sentences.en: Well, in a way, this kind of routine trial in this small town in Iowa became this larger philosophical debate over which version of Diane should be listened to.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从某种意义上说，爱荷华州这个小镇上的这场例行审判，演变成了一场更广泛的哲学辩论：到底应该听取哪个版本的黛安的话。

sentences.en: You know, Chris and Julie made the point that their mother had for years told them if she ever got dementia, they should be the ones to take care of her.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，克里斯和朱莉的观点是，她们的母亲多年来一直对她们说，如果她得了痴呆症，应该由她们来照顾她。

sentences.en: She trusted them to make the right decision for her.
sentences.zh: 她信任她们能为她做出正确的决定。

sentences.en: Denzel, on the other hand, argued that none of that really mattered because the version of Diane, who was sitting in front of them all, was saying something very different.
sentences.zh: 而另一方面，丹泽辩称这些都不重要，因为坐在大家面前的这个黛安，正在表达完全不同的意愿。

sentences.en: She was saying she wanted him.
sentences.zh: 她在说她想要他。

sentences.en: So in the end, it was a question of what does Diane really want?
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，问题在于黛安真正想要的是什么？

sentences.en: Is it what she's saying she wants there in the moment in court?
sentences.zh: 是她在法庭上当场表达的意愿吗？

sentences.en: Or is it what she said consistently for all the years before her mind became impaired?
sentences.zh: 还是她在大脑受损前多年里一直保持一致的说法？

sentences.en: And ultimately, what does the judge decide?
sentences.zh: 最终，法官做出了什么决定？

sentences.en: In the end, neither of those two sides wins.
sentences.zh: 最后，双方都没有赢。

sentences.en: The judge decides that Chris and Julie won't be suitable guardians, in part because they live out of state,
sentences.zh: 法官裁定克里斯和朱莉不适合担任监护人，部分原因是她们住在外州，

sentences.en: but also because they don't seem to be taking their mother's wishes into consideration when making decisions for her.
sentences.zh: 也是因为她们在为母亲做决定时似乎没有考虑母亲的意愿。

sentences.en: On the other hand, the judge thinks Denzel will be unsuitable because he really seems to underappreciate how sick Diane is.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，法官认为丹泽也不适合，因为他似乎严重低估了黛安的病情。

sentences.en: He says over and over in court that she's not sick at all, as far as he knows.
sentences.zh: 他在法庭上一再坚称，据他所知她根本没有生病。

sentences.en: So the judge takes this middle course and appoints one of Diane's friends, Marsha Losh, as the guardian.
sentences.zh: 因此，法官采取了折中方案，指定黛安的朋友玛莎·洛什担任监护人。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And what do both sides end up making of that middle course, starting with Denzel?
sentences.zh: 那么双方对这个折中方案最终作何感想？从丹泽开始吧。

sentences.en: I think he still feels liberated by the decision.
sentences.zh: 我想他依然觉得这个判决让他得到了解脱。

sentences.en: That's who Diane wanted.
sentences.zh: 那是黛安想要的人。

sentences.en: When they asked Diane who she liked to be her guardian, she said Marsha.
sentences.zh: 当他们问黛安希望谁来当她的监护人时，她说的是玛莎。

sentences.en: And of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: He's friendly with the woman who's appointed guardian.
sentences.zh: 他和被指定的监护人关系很好。

sentences.en: And with her permission, he gains the right to see Diane whenever he wants, also to move back into her house.
sentences.zh: 经她同意，他重新获得了随时探望黛安的权利，也可以搬回她的房子里居住。

sentences.en: I was there three times a day to see her when she was there, when I could.
sentences.zh: 只要有可能，她在那儿的时候我一天去三次看她。

sentences.en: Three times a day.
sentences.zh: 一天三次。

sentences.en: And so he kind of continues doing what he'd been doing before, visiting her every day, spending the day.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上是在继续他以前做的事，每天去看望她，陪伴她一整天。

sentences.en: But I mean, I knew she was getting worse.
sentences.zh: 但我的确知道她在恶化。

sentences.en: That dementia only went one way.
sentences.zh: 这种痴呆症只会越来越严重。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He does start to notice at this time that Diane isn't what she used to be.
sentences.zh: 此时他确实开始注意到黛安不如从前了。

sentences.en: Well, I'd help her put her makeup on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我会帮她化化妆。

sentences.en: And I think that was probably the first thing I noticed.
sentences.zh: 我想这大概是我注意到的第一件事。

sentences.en: It sort of starts with her makeup.
sentences.zh: 这有点从她的妆容开始。

sentences.en: I mean, she was a very attractive lady.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她是一位非常有魅力的女士。

sentences.en: She was a real lady.
sentences.zh: 她是一位真正的淑女。

sentences.en: And it bothered her that she couldn't, her hands, you know, were shaking and that.
sentences.zh: 而她的手，你知道的，一直在发抖什么的，这让她很苦恼。

sentences.en: And so I actually helped her put her makeup on.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上是我帮她化了妆。

sentences.en: I probably didn't do a real good job.
sentences.zh: 我可能做得不是很好。

sentences.en: But I helped her put her makeup on every morning.
sentences.zh: 但我每天早晨都帮她化好妆。

sentences.en: And as Diane's dementia got worse, she's moved to a different facility, a nursing home with a specialized memory care unit.
sentences.zh: 随着黛安的痴呆症日益恶化，她被转到了另一家机构，一家设有专门失智护理单元的疗养院。

sentences.en: But Denzel keeps visiting her there and his visits continue until 2020, the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但丹泽尔一直在那里探望她，他的探望一直持续到2020年大流行爆发。

sentences.en: The COVID.
sentences.zh: 也就是新冠疫情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When the COVID started, then, you know, I couldn't get her out of there anymore.
sentences.zh: 当新冠疫情开始时，你知道的，我就再也不能把她从那里接出来了。

sentences.en: Diane, some days seemed to understand what was going on, but other times seemed to know nothing of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 黛安有时似乎明白发生了什么，但其他时候对这场大流行似乎一无所知。

sentences.en: And it got to where it was hurt.
sentences.zh: 事情发展到了令人心碎的地步。

sentences.en: So she would, a few times, she said, I know you can get in here.
sentences.zh: 所以她有时会说，我知道你能进来。

sentences.en: You just don't want to.
sentences.zh: 你只是不想来。

sentences.en: You know, and that really hurt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真的很伤人。

sentences.en: Because she understood COVID at firSt.
sentences.zh: 因为起初她是理解新冠疫情的。

sentences.en: But then it got to where she didn't understand the COVID.
sentences.zh: 但后来发展到她不理解新冠疫情了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She accused Denzel of choosing not to visit her, of being allowed to come inside, but not wanting to.
sentences.zh: 她指责丹泽尔选择不来看她，明明被允许进来却不愿进来。

sentences.en: We just had a really good few years there.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里度过了非常美好的几年。

sentences.en: But that all ended.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都结束了。

sentences.en: That dementia is, to me, is worse than cancer.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，痴呆症比癌症还要糟糕。

sentences.en: And then eventually, it became less clear to Denzel that Diane always knew who he was.
sentences.zh: 后来，丹泽尔越来越不确定黛安是否还总是认得他是谁。

sentences.en: And it was around that time, he says, that he stopped visiting.
sentences.zh: 他说，正是在那个时候，他停止了探望。

sentences.en: And it's an untidy goodbye.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不完美的告别。

sentences.en: And it's incomplete.
sentences.zh: 而且是不完整的。

sentences.en: It's just one day, a visit is hard.
sentences.zh: 只是有一天，探望变得很艰难。

sentences.en: And then that's the last that Denzel ever sees Diane again.
sentences.zh: 然后，那是丹泽尔最后一次见到黛安。

sentences.en: So, let's return to Chris and to Julie.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们回到克里斯和朱莉身上。

sentences.en: What do they do after they find out about the judge's decision in the Guardian case?
sentences.zh: 在得知法官对监护权案的裁决后，他们做了什么？

sentences.en: So, Chris and Julie go back to their respective homes.
sentences.zh: 于是，克里斯和朱莉回到了各自的家中。

sentences.en: And immediately, they start working on an appeal.
sentences.zh: 他们立刻开始着手准备上诉。

sentences.en: But they also continue this relentless sort of effort to get in touch with their mother.
sentences.zh: 但他们也继续进行这种不懈的努力，试图与母亲取得联系。

sentences.en: But their calls wouldn't be put through.
sentences.zh: 但他们的电话根本转接不进去。

sentences.en: They'd get friends to call, too, sometimes.
sentences.zh: 有时他们还会让朋友帮忙打电话。

sentences.en: And just try desperately to get word of Diane.
sentences.zh: 拼命地想要得到黛安的消息。

sentences.en: And none of that worked until...
sentences.zh: 然而这些努力都无济于事，直到……

sentences.en: This is Erin.
sentences.zh: 我是艾琳。

sentences.en: Can I help you?
sentences.zh: 有什么我可以帮您的吗？

sentences.en: Hi, Erin.
sentences.zh: 你好，艾琳。

sentences.en: Can I speak to Diane Norrelius, please?
sentences.zh: 请帮我转黛安·诺雷利乌斯，好吗？

sentences.en: Yes, just a minute.
sentences.zh: 好的，请稍等。

sentences.en: One day, Julie's friend Mary calls the nursing home.
sentences.zh: 有一天，朱莉的朋友玛丽给疗养院打了电话。

sentences.en: And to everyone's surprise, she's put through to Diane.
sentences.zh: 出乎所有人意料的是，电话竟然转给了黛安。

sentences.en: Hello, Diane.
sentences.zh: 喂，黛安。

sentences.en: This is Mary.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽。

sentences.en: I called you last week.
sentences.zh: 我上周给你打过电话。

sentences.en: How are you doing today?
sentences.zh: 你今天过得怎么样？

sentences.en: You're getting better.
sentences.zh: 你在好转呢。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Mary and Diane were able to talk a couple of times.
sentences.zh: 玛丽和黛安通了几次电话。

sentences.en: And it was clear that Diane's cognition was very diminished at this point.
sentences.zh: 很明显，此时黛安的认知能力已经严重退化。

sentences.en: She seemed confused.
sentences.zh: 她显得很困惑。

sentences.en: A lot of what she said didn't make a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 她说的很多话都让人有些费解。

sentences.en: But what was clear was that she was unhappy where she was living, in this basement unit of the local nursing home.
sentences.zh: 但显而易见的是，她对自己的居住环境很不满意，也就是当地疗养院的地下一层。

sentences.en: So I called your daughter, Julie, and she's finding you a different place to live.
sentences.zh: 所以我给你的女儿朱莉打了电话，她正在为你找一个不同的住处。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Oh, my goodness.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: I was able to listen to one of the calls.
sentences.zh: 我有幸听了其中一个录音。

sentences.en: And on it, Mary tells Diane that she's been in touch with Chris and Julie, and that they're going to try to get her moved to a different, better facility.
sentences.zh: 电话里，玛丽告诉黛安，她已经联系了克里斯和朱莉，他们正设法把她转到一个更好、更合适的新机构。

sentences.en: Well, don't cry.
sentences.zh: 好了，别哭。

sentences.en: Don't cry.
sentences.zh: 别哭。

sentences.en: Diane just breaks down in tears, and she says it would be so wonderful.
sentences.zh: 黛安当场泪崩，她说这真是太好了。

sentences.en: And she's so happy to hear that her daughters are maybe going to help her.
sentences.zh: 听到女儿们可能会来帮她，她高兴极了。

sentences.en: They're going to come and see you as soon as they can, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她们会尽快来看你的。

sentences.en: Is that okay?
sentences.zh: 这样行吗？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 行，当然行。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然行。

sentences.en: Have them come and see you.
sentences.zh: 让她们来看你吧。

sentences.en: But at the end of the call...
sentences.zh: 但在通话快结束时……

sentences.en: Okay, Diane, I'm going to let you go.
sentences.zh: 好了，黛安，我要挂电话了。

sentences.en: I'm going to call Julie right now.
sentences.zh: 我马上给朱莉打电话。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And then I'll call you back.
sentences.zh: 然后我再给你打回来。

sentences.en: Thank you, sweetheart.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，亲爱的。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: You're the sweetheart.
sentences.zh: 你才是小甜心。

sentences.en: Diane forgets to hang up.
sentences.zh: 黛安忘记挂断电话了。

sentences.en: And Mary just sort of stays on the line for a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 玛丽就在线停留了几分钟。

sentences.en: And you can hear Diane crying softly in the background and then sitting in silence for a while.
sentences.zh: 你可以听到黛安在背景音里轻轻啜泣，然后静静地坐了一会儿。

sentences.en: And then you can hear a nurse come in, and she asks Diane if she's okay.
sentences.zh: 接着可以听到一个护士走进来，问黛安有没有事。

sentences.en: She tells the nurse, they hate me.
sentences.zh: 她对护士说，他们讨厌我。

sentences.en: They call me bad things.
sentences.zh: 他们用难听的话骂我。

sentences.en: So in September 2020, a court finally agrees to Chris and Julie's request that Diane be moved to a more specialized facility in Omaha.
sentences.zh: 因此在2020年9月，法院终于同意了克里斯和朱莉的请求，将黛安转移到奥马哈的一家专业护理机构。

sentences.en: Almost immediately after arriving, she is put on hospice care.
sentences.zh: 刚一入住，她几乎立刻就被安排接受安宁疗护。

sentences.en: Doctors decide that she is dying and doesn't have very long to live.
sentences.zh: 医生判定她已经病危，时日无多。

sentences.en: And it was then that a judge finally signs this order granting Chris and Julie the right to see their mother for the first time in over two years because of the state Diane's in.
sentences.zh: 正因黛安目前的状况，法官终于签署了这项命令，准许克里斯和朱莉在两年多来首次探望她们的母亲。

sentences.en: Chris is immune compromised and decided that it wasn't safe for her to travel during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 克里斯免疫力受损，因此认为大流行期间出行对母亲并不安全。

sentences.en: But Julie gets in her truck and she drives nine hours to Nebraska.
sentences.zh: 但朱莉坐上了卡车，驱车九个小时赶往内布拉斯加州。

sentences.en: Walking through her threshold.
sentences.zh: 跨进家门的那一刻。

sentences.en: I mean, the anxiety, the fear of, you know, I haven't seen mom for, what, Chris, three years?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那种焦虑，那种恐惧，你知道的，我有多久没见妈妈了？克里斯，三年吗？

sentences.en: I hadn't seen my mother.
sentences.zh: 我一直没能见到我的母亲。

sentences.en: And she ends up spending four, as she describes them, completely pleasant and wonderful days with Diane.
sentences.zh: 最后，她和黛安度过了用她的话说“完全愉快而美好”的四天。

sentences.en: I went in and mom was in bed.
sentences.zh: 我走进去，妈妈正躺在床上。

sentences.en: She was very weak.
sentences.zh: 她非常虚弱。

sentences.en: But I sat beside her.
sentences.zh: 但我坐在她身旁。

sentences.en: She sat up.
sentences.zh: 她坐了起来。

sentences.en: We talked.
sentences.zh: 我们交谈。

sentences.en: We hugged.
sentences.zh: 我们拥抱。

sentences.en: We kissed.
sentences.zh: 我们接吻。

sentences.en: We giggled.
sentences.zh: 我们咯咯笑着。

sentences.en: And she was so happy.
sentences.zh: 她开心极了。

sentences.en: And then she laid down and I tucked her in under her little blankie.
sentences.zh: 然后她躺下，我帮她掖好盖在小毯子下面。

sentences.en: And she said, oh, stay here by me.
sentences.zh: 她说，哦，留下来陪我。

sentences.en: Stay here.
sentences.zh: 留在这里。

sentences.en: And so she held my hand and I just laid down beside her.
sentences.zh: 于是她握着我的手，我就这样躺在她身旁。

sentences.en: And sometimes Julie says, Diane seems to maybe ask about Denzel.
sentences.zh: 朱莉说，有时候黛安似乎会问起丹泽尔。

sentences.en: She asks, where's that man?
sentences.zh: 她问，那个男人在哪里？

sentences.en: Where's that man?
sentences.zh: 那个男人在哪里？

sentences.en: A few times.
sentences.zh: 问了好几次。

sentences.en: But she never calls him by name.
sentences.zh: 但她从不叫他的名字。

sentences.en: I can't tell you how hard it was to have to leave that last day.
sentences.zh: 我无法形容最后一天离开时有多么艰难。

sentences.en: When I left, the feeling I had was that this is how it should have been from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 当我离开时，给我的感觉是，这一切本该从一开始就是这样的。

sentences.en: In January of 2021, Chris and Julie are granted guardianship of Diane.
sentences.zh: 2021年1月，克里斯和朱莉获得了黛安的监护权。

sentences.en: And they call each other.
sentences.zh: 她们互相给对方打电话。

sentences.en: They can't believe this has finally happened.
sentences.zh: 简直不敢相信这一切终于发生了。

sentences.en: They start planning a trip together to see their mother.
sentences.zh: 她们开始计划一起去探望母亲。

sentences.en: But four days later, before they could take that trip, Diane dies at the nursing home.
sentences.zh: 但四天后，还没等她们成行，黛安就在疗养院去世了。

sentences.en: Katie, it occurs to me that in the story that you have just told, everybody involved was hurt in some way.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，我突然觉得，在你刚才讲的故事里，涉事的每个人都在某种程度上受到了伤害。

sentences.en: And hurt deeply.
sentences.zh: 而且伤得很深。

sentences.en: The daughters.
sentences.zh: 女儿们。

sentences.en: Densel.
sentences.zh: 丹泽尔。

sentences.en: Diane.
sentences.zh: 黛安。

sentences.en: So how do you think about why there was so much pain in this story?
sentences.zh: 那么，你觉得为什么这个故事里会有这么多的痛苦？

sentences.en: Is this really about bad decisions made by the people that we have been talking about?
sentences.zh: 这真的是因为我们讨论过的这些人做出了错误的决定吗？

sentences.en: Or is this about a bad system that we have for handling people with dementia?
sentences.zh: 还是因为我们处理痴呆症患者的体制存在弊端？

sentences.en: Or is it both?
sentences.zh: 抑或是两者皆有？

sentences.en: I think as a journalist, I often write stories where there are, in the end, good guys and bad guys.
sentences.zh: 我想作为一名记者，我经常写这样的故事：到最后，总能分出好人与坏人。

sentences.en: And that's not how I felt in this case.
sentences.zh: 但在这个案子里，我并没有这种感觉。

sentences.en: I really felt that everyone involved in this story was kind of arguing and fighting in good faith.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得，这个故事里的每个人其实都是出于善意在争论和抗争。

sentences.en: Everyone loved Diane.
sentences.zh: 每个人都爱黛安。

sentences.en: I think, you know, in part, there are weaknesses in the system.
sentences.zh: 我认为，部分原因在于体制的缺陷。

sentences.en: I mean, if you look at someone who has dementia, that person might live with the diagnosis for years, slowly deteriorating.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你看一个患有痴呆症的人，这个人可能会带着诊断生活多年，病情慢慢恶化。

sentences.en: And there's no clear and obvious and easy to measure point at which a person with dementia loses the ability to do something for herself and then loses the legal right to do it.
sentences.zh: 并没有一个清晰、显眼且易于衡量的节点，能标志着一个失智患者在某个时刻失去了照顾自己的能力，进而失去了这样做的法律权利。

sentences.en: I think that's just an inherent difficulty with the disease.
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是该疾病本身固有的难点所在。

sentences.en: The medical system can try and the court system can try to locate that point, but it's not going to be easy.
sentences.zh: 医疗系统和法院系统可以尝试去寻找那个节点，但这绝非易事。

sentences.en: And certainly a person with dementia, a person like Diane, can remember things and forget things and remember again in the course of a day.
sentences.zh: 而且毫无疑问，一个痴呆症患者，像黛安这样的人，在一天当中完全可能记起一些事，忘记一些事，然后又再次记起。

sentences.en: So what do you do with that?
sentences.zh: 所以你该拿这怎么办呢？
