sentences.en: But I think beyond that, in many ways, Denzel and Diane's daughters were just living with different versions of the same woman.
sentences.zh: 但我认为除此之外，在许多方面，丹泽尔和黛安的女儿们只是生活在同一个女人的不同版本之中。

sentences.en: And I think, given how they knew Diane, this is understandable.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，考虑到他们了解黛安的方式，这是可以理解的。

sentences.en: The daughters were committed to the then version of their mother, the pre-dementia version of their mother, the one they'd lived with for decades,
sentences.zh: 女儿们执着于她们母亲当年的那个版本，也就是患痴呆症之前的母亲版本，那个她们与之共同生活了数十年的母亲，

sentences.en: the one who had been clear about what she wanted at the end of her life.
sentences.zh: 那个在生命行将结束时清楚表达过自己意愿的人。

sentences.en: And they felt obliged to, even when that woman seemed to disappear, to recall her and to honor her, what she wanted.
sentences.zh: 她们觉得有责任去怀念她，去尊重她想要的，即使那个女人看起来已经消失了。

sentences.en: And Denzel, on the other hand, only had the woman who was sitting in front of him at the moment.
sentences.zh: 而另一方面，丹泽尔面对的只有此刻坐在他面前的这个女人。

sentences.en: And he felt that he loved her and that the right thing to do was to listen to her, to listen to what she was saying and to take it at face value,
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己爱她，正确做法就是听取她的意见，听听她在说些什么，并按字面意思去理解，

sentences.en: not as some pathological symptom of a cognitive impairment.
sentences.zh: 而不是把它当作认知障碍的某种病理症状。

sentences.en: And so he was, in a way, advocating for the Diane who was diminished.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，他是在为那个认知能力退化的黛安发声。

sentences.en: And I think, even amongst academics who debate this, you know, this is a contested subject.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，即使在探讨这个问题的学者当中，你也知道，这是一个备受争议的话题。

sentences.en: Who's the authentic person?
sentences.zh: 谁才是真正的本人？

sentences.en: Who, in this case, was the real Diane?
sentences.zh: 在这个案例中，谁才是真正的黛安？

sentences.en: I mean, have you come to a conclusion of your own after spending all this time with the family, with Denzel, and with the documents?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在花光了这么多时间与这个家庭、与丹泽尔以及与这些文件接触之后，你得出了自己的结论吗？

sentences.en: I mean, which one was the real Diane?
sentences.zh: 我是说，哪一个才是真正的黛安？

sentences.en: The one the kids remembered and wanted to honor or the one who fell in love with Denzel?
sentences.zh: 是孩子们记忆中并想要去怀念的那个人，还是那个爱上丹泽尔的人？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's hard to say who the real Diane was, but I do know that as a society, with our medical system and our legal system as they are,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为很难说谁才是真正的黛安，但我确实知道，作为一个社会，随着我们的医疗系统和法律系统现状如此，

sentences.en: we're moving in the direction of honoring Denzel's version of Diane.
sentences.zh: 我们正在朝着尊重丹泽尔版本的黛安这个方向发展。

sentences.en: It used to be, you know, in the early 20th century, that just having a diagnosis of dementia basically meant that you were stripped of all your decision-making power,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在20世纪早期，仅仅被诊断出患有痴呆症，基本上就意味着你被剥夺了所有的决策权，

sentences.en: stripped of all your civil liberties, and put under the control of other people.
sentences.zh: 被剥夺了所有的公民自由，并被置于其他人的控制之下。

sentences.en: And we've moved away from that system, and we've moved towards a world in which we hope even people with significant disabilities and impairments can live with some autonomy.
sentences.zh: 我们已经远离了那个系统，并朝着这样一个世界迈进：我们希望即使是患有严重残疾和认知障碍的人也能带着一定的自主权生活。

sentences.en: And in the case of dementia, that means increasingly listening to what a person with dementia says she wants,
sentences.zh: 而在痴呆症的案例中，这意味着越来越多地倾听一个患有痴呆症的人说她想要什么，

sentences.en: even if it's different from what she said she wanted for decades and decades of her life.
sentences.zh: 即使这与她几十年来一直说她想要的东西不同。

sentences.en: And I think that is understandable from a, you know, political or legal standpoint, but very, very challenging for the adult children of people with this disease.
sentences.zh: 我认为从政治或法律的角度来看，这是可以理解的，但对于患病者的成年子女来说，这非常非常具有挑战性。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because they have to live with the reality that the now version of their mother or their father or their sister or their brother is the one that the system privileges and prioritizes.
sentences.zh: 因为他们必须接受这样一个现实：系统所特许和优先考虑的是他们母亲、父亲、姐妹或兄弟现在的这个版本。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I think it can be terrifying for, you know, the rest of us too.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，对于我们其他人来说，这也可能会让人感到极其恐惧。

sentences.en: We can tell our children what we want to happen to us when we're older.
sentences.zh: 我们可以告诉孩子们，当我们老了之后希望发生什么。

sentences.en: In the event that we get sick, we can write out documents outlining our wishes, but in the end, they might just not be listened to because in the throes of the disease,
sentences.zh: 万一生病了，我们可以写下概述我们愿望的文件，但到头来，这些愿望可能根本不会被听取，因为在疾病的发作期间，

sentences.en: we might change our minds.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会改变主意。

sentences.en: And that can be very scary.
sentences.zh: 这可能会非常吓人。

sentences.en: You know, I feel like I know who I am and it's,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我感觉我很清楚我是谁，而且，

sentences.en: it's frightening the thought that some different impaired version of me might actually have both the ethical and the legal authority to usurp what I decide I want.
sentences.zh: 一想到某个不同且认知受损的我竟然真正拥有伦理和法律上的权力来篡夺我决定想要的东西，这就让人感到害怕。

sentences.en: Well, Katie, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，凯蒂，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们非常感激。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。
